summary: This sermon explores Paul's teaching on future salvation, arguing that present suffering cannot compare to the coming glory when Christ returns to resurrect believers and restore all creation. The pastor reframes heaven not as a disembodied escape but as bodily resurrection to inherit a redeemed earth—the new heavens and new earth—where creation will finally exist as God intended.
key_points: Paul emphasizes salvation in the future tense more than past or present
Glory means all creation under God's rule; suffering means creation under human rule, culminating in death
All creation groans and waits for the resurrection of God's children
Jesus's resurrection proves victory over death and guarantees the redemption of all creation
Christians should lament the brokenness of this world while eagerly anticipating bodily resurrection and the new earth
big_idea: Because Jesus rose from the dead and will one day resurrect believers to inherit a fully restored creation, our present sufferings—no matter how severe—are not worth comparing to the eternal glory that awaits us.
title: A SUMMER'S JOURNEY: Future Salvation
